argument:
I ran the numbers before writing this, and they refute the core of my own pitch. Withdrawn.

On point 1 (no edge at mid-range): confirmed and worse than stated. Regressing log EWC/ACWI on log Brent over the full year (yfinance daily, through 2026-08-07 close) gives a crude-implied fair ratio of 0.3787 vs. actual 0.3797 — a +0.27% residual. There is no lag, no catch-up, no dislocation. The ratio is exactly where crude says it should be. My 'room to the 52-week high' framing described a range, not a signal. Conceded in full.

On point 2 (correlated wrapper): confirmed empirically. Correlation of EWC/ACWI returns to IWD/IWF returns is +0.35 over 1Y daily, +0.55 over the last 60 days, and +0.51 at monthly frequency over 2Y. Correlation of the pair to crude is +0.18 daily (1Y), +0.13 over the last 60d — and +0.09 at monthly frequency. Log-log beta of the ratio to Brent is 0.081: a 9.5% Brent month implies +0.73% on the ratio. My central claim — 'cleanest listed expression of the Hormuz oil shock' — is empirically false. EWC/ACWI is a low-beta-to-crude vehicle whose dominant recent co-movement is with the very value/growth factor I flagged as crowded at the 94th percentile. Buying it here is buying the extension through a wrapper, exactly as charged. If the desk wants the oil shock, the commodities seat owns CL outright with ~12x the beta; if it wants the factor, that entry is crowded. Neither route needs this pair.

On point 3 (hawkish-BoC corridor): stands, and my own data makes it worse than the challenger framed it. Monthly correlation of EWC/ACWI to CAD (CAD=X) over 2Y is -0.28 — the wrong sign. CAD strength is largely a USD-weakness proxy, and a weak USD lifts ACWI's non-US sleeve; historically a hawkish-BoC/CAD-rally leg has coincided with the ratio FALLING, not rising. So the rate-differential leg of my thesis wasn't just narrow — its empirical sign on the instrument is negative. Combined with the ~33% financials weight vs. ~17% energy, the construction fights the thesis on two channels.

What survives: the regime read itself (inflation scare, two-sided hike risk under a Warsh Fed, stagflation-lite tape) and the challenger's concession that short ACWI/short mega-cap growth-ad exposure expresses it. But a correct regime view attached to the wrong instrument is not a pitch — it's a note for the desk run.

Per protocol, conviction revised 6 → 4: entry at crude-implied fair value, dominant correlation with a crowded factor, wrong-signed CAD leg, and a -2.7% stop a Sunday ceasefire gap in Brent will not honor. Below 5, I withdraw. If Brent holds >$80 into September and the ratio retraces to a genuine dislocation (z ≤ -0.5 vs. crude-implied fair value), I will re-originate with the factor-correlation problem addressed in the hedge construction.
